item.description:

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM HST Sun Oct 25 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located a few hundred miles west-southwest of Acapulco,
Mexico, and on Tropical Storm Olana, located several hundred miles
west-southwest of Johnston Atoll.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Olana are issued under
WMO header WTPA33 KNHC and under AWIPS header HFOTCPCP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Olana are issued under
WMO header WTPA23 KNHC and under AWIPS header HFOTCMCP3.

$$

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Olana (CP3/CP032026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...OLANA HOLDING STEADY... As of 11:00 PM HST Sun Oct 25 the center of Olana was located near 14.9, -176.6 with movement E at 7 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1002 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 40 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Olana Public Advisory Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Sun Oct 25 2026 
303 
WTPA33 PHFO 260830
TCPCP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Olana Advisory Number   4
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP032026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Sun Oct 25 2026
 
...OLANA HOLDING STEADY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.9N 176.6W
ABOUT 490 MI...785 KM WSW OF JOHNSTON ISLAND
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...E OR 95 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in Johnston Atoll should monitor the progress of this
system.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Olana was 
located near latitude 14.9 North, longitude 176.6 West. Olana is 
moving toward the east near 7 mph (11 km/h) and a general eastward 
motion is expected during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Gradual weakening is expected and Olana is now forecast to become a 
remnant low in a day or so.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Tropical Storm Olana Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Sun Oct 25 2026 
000
WTPA43 PHFO 260831
TCDCP3
 
Tropical Storm Olana Discussion Number   4
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP032026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Sun Oct 25 2026
 
Olana continues to produce deep convection with cold cloud tops 
near -80C near and to the northeast of the low-level center, as 
southwesterly wind shear begins to increase. The overall convective 
pattern has not changed significantly, and the convective shield has 
remained in a fairly steady state over the past several hours. The 
latest subjective and objective intensity values range between 
28-35 kt. Using these estimates and steady satellite appearance, 
the initial intensity is held at 35 kt for this advisory, although 
that could be generous.
 
The system is forecast to move into even stronger southwesterly 
vertical wind shear which, coupled with dry air entrainment, should 
induce a weakening trend. Given the increasingly hostile 
environmental conditions along the forecast track, the official 
forecast shows Olana degenerating into a remnant low by 36 hours and 
dissipating into an elongated trough by day 3. The official 
intensity forecast lies near the upper end of the guidance in the 
short term before trending toward the latest consensus aids through 
the remainder of the forecast period.
 
The initial motion is eastward, or 095/6 kt. A generally 
eastward track is expected during the next couple of days as the 
cyclone is steered by the flow along the southern periphery of 
a trough. The official track forecast is similar to the previous 
advisory, but just slightly slower. Based on the latest guidance, 
Olana is expected to dissipate prior to reaching Johnston Atoll.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
